source.title: A safety realignment framework via subspace-oriented model fusion for large language models
source.authors: Xin Yi; Shunfan Zheng; Linlin Wang; Xiaoling Wang; Liang He

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign task-specific fine-tuning affects safety, using task fine-tuning and harmlessness preference evaluations rather than the original study’s method. It also evaluates attack prompts, but does not measure token-position KL or test the other proposed bypasses.
record.gate_note: The study reports safety outcomes after fine-tuning on downstream task data described as instruction data, and safety outcomes under attack prompts. It does not test harmful-example fine-tuning, token-position KL, compliant prefill, decoding changes, or whether safety is carried by a small set of weights. Full-FT Table 3 is too flattened to assign its task-specific values reliably; the text does report an aggregate safety reduction. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: Fine-tunes a DPO safety-aligned WizardLM-7B (LoRA) and TinyLlama-1.1B (full FT) on benign task data: Alpaca in Chinese, English and Hindi, CodeAlpaca, and GSM8K. It reports harmlessness preference rates against the aligned model on five harm benchmarks. This uses a different method and measure (a GPT-3.5 pairwise judge) aimed at V2. Most of the paper evaluates its own realignment method, SOMF.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that benign downstream fine-tuning compromises safety and that SOMF restores it for single and fused models while preserving task performance. The residual weakness under CoT and CoU attacks with Full-FT belongs to the SOMF-realigned model.
record.recipe_differences: Tests benign downstream task fine-tuning and evaluates a learned-mask model-fusion realignment method; it does not reproduce the original harmful-example or token-position-KL methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety outcomes vary by downstream task, training strategy (PEFT versus Full-FT), safety evaluation dataset, and attack prompt. The authors report Full-FT declines under CoT and CoU attacks.

fits_no_version.finding: Pearson correlation of W_v changes between SFT and realigned models is lowest in early layers (layer 2 PEFT, layer 5 Full-FT). The authors read this as a denser concentration of safety-critical parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-relevant parameter shifts from benign fine-tuning concentrate in early layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Fused-model safety generally declines as more benign-fine-tuned models are merged (Fig. 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Merging more benign task models compounds safety loss.

record.problems: Safety is assessed using GPT-3.5-turbo pairwise preference judgments rather than direct refusal or harmful-completion rates. The Full-FT table is flattened in the supplied text, preventing reliable assignment of its task-level scores. The authors note resource constraints limiting experiments to models up to 7B and dependence on the quality and representativeness of safety preference data.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 Full-FT task-specific values were not extracted because the supplied flattened layout does not reliably associate the values with task and evaluation-dataset columns. Figure 6 attack-specific values are recorded as figure-only because the text gives no exact numbers. Table 4's SOMF-realigned rows are omitted because they measure the realignment method's outcomes rather than the effect of benign fine-tuning itself.

untested.parts: Carefully selected benign data (e.g. data chosen to be near harmful examples) is not tested. The Full-FT Table 3 values can't be read reliably from the text.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling or decoding attacks. Attack prompts are evaluated only in Fig. 6, without readable values or a no-attack baseline.
The learned mask and layer-correlation analysis do not establish that a small set of weights carries safety.

missing.what: SFT vs Aligned harmlessness rates on HarmfulQA, Shadow-Alignment and DangerousQA, for PEFT and Full-FT. Full-FT DangerousQA SFT exceeds aligned.
Full-FT TinyLlama SFT vs Aligned on CATQA and BeaverTails. The flattened table is not reliably readable, but the text cites an SFT average of 36.23.
Aligned and SFT models under CoT, CoU and suffix attack prompts; CoU is said to be the hardest for the SFT model.

record.verdict_notes: The measure is a GPT-3.5 pairwise harmlessness score against the base model (wins minus losses over total), not a refusal or attack-success rate. The base models were uncensored or weakly aligned and were safety-aligned by the authors with DPO on PKU-SafeRLHF. Aligned Full-FT reference scores are low, so drops there are hard to read. Non-English task data included 50k English instructions. The reader's V4 label is dropped because those rows evaluate the study's own method.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test carefully selected benign examples as a separate category; task-specific fine-tuning results are not reported with reliably assignable Full-FT task-by-task values.
No per-token KL or other comparison of aligned and base output distributions across response positions.
No compliant-token prefilling or decoding changes. Attack-prompt results concern the realigned model and do not provide a direct attack-versus-no-attack refusal rate.
The study learns a safety-related mask, but does not establish that a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether the data or training objective produces shallow safety.
Does not test training intended to spread safety beyond early response tokens.
